conceptBreakdown.title: Origin of Life: Primordial Earth & Chemical Evolution

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Earth formed ~4.5 billion years ago with a hot, reducing atmosphere lacking free O2. Oparin and Haldane proposed that life arose through chemical evolution from simple inorganic molecules to organic monomers, polymers, and protobionts. Stanley Miller and Harold Urey (1953) proved this experimentally by synthesizing amino acids in a closed spark-discharge apparatus at 800°C.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PRIMORDIAL EARTH CONDITIONS
                                      │
  No Free Oxygen (O₂ ABSENT) ──► Reducing Atmosphere (CH₄, NH₃, H₂O vapor, H₂)
                                      │
  High Temperature + UV Radiation + Lightning ──► Chemical Evolution (Abiogenesis)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 1.1 Primordial Earth Atmosphere
- The Universe originated $\approx 20\text{ billion years ago}$ via the Big Bang.
- Earth was formed $\approx 4.5\text{ billion years ago}$ with no protective ozone layer and no free oxygen (reducing atmosphere).
- Molten mass released **$\text{CH}_4, \text{NH}_3, \text{H}_2\text{O vapor}$, and $\text{H}_2$**.
- UV rays from the sun broke down $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ into Hydrogen and Oxygen ($H_2$ escaped into space).

### 1.2 Theories on the Origin of Life
1. **Theory of Spontaneous Generation (Abiogenesis)**: Life arose from decaying non-living matter. Debunked by **Louis Pasteur** using swan-neck flasks, establishing **Biogenesis** (life arises only from pre-existing life).
2. **Panspermia / Cosmozoic Theory**: Spores of life traveled across interstellar space to Earth.
3. **Oparin-Haldane Chemosynthetic Theory**: First forms of life arose through spontaneous chemical evolution:
   $$\text{Inorganic Gases} \longrightarrow \text{Organic Monomers} \longrightarrow \text{Complex Polymers} \longrightarrow \text{Protobionts} \longrightarrow \text{Living Cells}$$

### 1.3 The Miller-Urey Experiment (1953)

```
                      MILLER-UREY EXPERIMENTAL APPARATUS
                      
         Tungsten Electrodes (Spark Discharge 800°C)
                            │
         Gases: CH₄ : NH₃ : H₂ : H₂O vapor (Ratio 2 : 2 : 1 : 2)
                            │
         Condenser (Cooling Circulating Water)
                            │
         Liquid Trap ──► Produced Amino Acids (Glycine, Alanine, Aspartic Acid)
```

- **Protobiont Precursors**:
  - **Coacervates (Oparin)**: Non-membranous colloidal aggregates of proteins and polysaccharides; grew by absorption but lacked lipid membranes and could not reproduce.
  - **Microspheres (Sidney Fox)**: Proteinoids bounded by semi-permeable lipid-like membranes; exhibited osmotic swelling and binary-like budding.
  - **First Cellular Life**: Emerged $\approx 2.0\text{ billion years ago}$ as anaerobic, heterotrophic unicellular organisms.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Haldane's Hot Dilute Soup
conceptBreakdown.title: Haldane's Hot Dilute Soup
conceptBreakdown.content: J.B.S. Haldane described the ancient oceans as a 'hot dilute soup' (pre-biotic broth) where organic compounds accumulated in the absence of free molecular oxygen and microorganisms that would otherwise degrade them.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Non-Enzymatic RNA Polymerization
conceptBreakdown.title: Non-Enzymatic RNA Polymerization
conceptBreakdown.content: Clay minerals such as Montmorillonite can catalyze the non-enzymatic polymerization of activated ribonucleotides into oligomers, supporting the transition from prebiotic chemistry to the RNA World.
